newsitem.title: USA: Northrop sees $90 mln Q4 pre-tax charge.
newsitem.headline: Northrop sees $90 mln Q4 pre-tax charge.

text.p: Northrop Grumman Corp said Wednesday it plans to close four plants and cut about 755 jobs, resulting in a pre-tax charge of $90 million in its fourth quarter of 1996.

The company said in a statement the move was part of its strategy of consolidation and streamlining to remain competitive. The $90 million charge includes a $60 million write-down for the closure of facilities and a $30 million charge related to the lay-offs and related closure costs.

"We regret that these actions will result in the loss of jobs, but they are necessary if we are to meet the affordability demands of our customers and win new business," said Kent Kresa, company chairman, president and chief executive officer.
All told, the defense company will lay off about 1,100 workers in the plant closings, although new jobs in some plants will reduce that net number to 755, the company said.
The brunt of the layoffs will be felt in California, New York and Florida.

In the company's Hawthorne, Calif., plant, which employs 770 workers, 530 people will be laid off while the remaining 240 will be offered transfers. The Hawthorne plant, which designs and produces electronic sensors, navigation and guidance systems and anti-tank weapons, will close by the end of 1997.

By the middle of the year Northrop plans to close its plant on New York's Long Island, with 330 of the 450 employees losing their jobs. The remaining 120 workers will be offered transfers. The Long Island plant makes electronic test and targeting equipment.
In Stuart, Fla., about half of the 500-strong work force will loose their jobs, with the balance offered transfers. The plant, which makes small aircraft structures, will close at the end of 1998.

More jobs might be lost at the company's Perry, Ga., facility. That facility will close in the coming 18-24 months. If the company won new commercial business for which it has bid, those workers would be relocated to a new smaller plant in Georgia. Without the new business, workers would be transfered to other facilities. A decision is expected by the middle of the year.
The company said it will be adding jobs at plants in Texas, Georgia, Illinois and Pennsylvania, thereby reducing the net job reductions to 755.
The Northrop plant to be closed on Long Island is located at Great River. Its three other plants on Long Island were unaffected by the restructuring.
